title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Illinois Wesleyan rituals and recurring events, from pineapple pats and fountain chalking to finals-week food and fall-semester gatherings.

cards.title: Write a Goal, Then Find Your Name
cards.subtitle: A four-year chalk cycle around Aspiration Fountain
cards.notes: During Turning Titan, chalk a college goal by the fountain; before Commencement, return to see faculty and staff honor graduates by name.
cards.short_summary: First-year ambitions and graduating-class names temporarily transform the same campus pavement.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan states that first-year students chalk college goals around Aspiration Fountain during orientation and that faculty and staff later chalk graduates’ names there before Commencement.
cards.access_notes: The first-year activity occurs during Turning Titan; the graduate-name display is installed in the lead-up to Commencement.

cards.title: Pat the Pineapple on the Way Out
cards.subtitle: A stone symbol marks the passage from student to alumnus
cards.notes: Watch for the stone pineapple at Commencement and give it the customary pat while crossing the stage into the alumni community.
cards.short_summary: Graduates complete their Illinois Wesleyan passage with an unexpectedly tropical stone landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan documents that seniors pat a stone pineapple while crossing the Commencement stage, symbolizing their transition into the Titan alumni community.
cards.access_notes: Participation is tied to the University’s Commencement ceremony and its graduating seniors.

cards.title: Let the President Serve Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Finals Week turns pancakes into an evening ritual
cards.notes: Take a finals study break for pancakes, eggs, sausage and tots served by the University president and other administrators.
cards.short_summary: Administrators swap official duties for breakfast service during the fall examination rush.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan identifies Late Night Breakfast as an annual fall Finals Week tradition featuring breakfast food served to students by the president and other administrators.
cards.access_notes: Held late at night during fall-semester Finals Week; the public traditions page does not provide the next event’s exact time or venue.

cards.title: Pause Finals for a PB&J
cards.subtitle: A second late-night Finals Week food custom
cards.notes: Step away from studying for a peanut-butter-and-jelly sandwich and snacks when the campus stages its Finals Week PB&J Night.
cards.short_summary: The familiar packed-lunch sandwich becomes a named nighttime examination-week tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan describes PB&J Night as a Finals Week tradition where students take a late-night study break for peanut-butter-and-jelly sandwiches and other snacks.
cards.access_notes: Held late at night during Finals Week; the public traditions page does not list the next date, time or allergen arrangements.

cards.title: End Orientation on a Climbing Wall
cards.subtitle: Turning Titan closes with rides, inflatables and food
cards.notes: Finish fall orientation at the campus carnival; look for rides, a climbing wall, large inflatables and food on the final evening.
cards.short_summary: The orientation finale replaces another meeting with a full-scale outdoor carnival.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan says Titan Carnival gathers the campus community on the final evening of fall orientation, with rides, a climbing wall, jumbo inflatables and food.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for the final evening of Turning Titan; individual attractions may carry their own participation requirements.

cards.title: Meet the Whole Club Roster at Once
cards.subtitle: Registered student organizations take over the Quad
cards.notes: Walk the Quad, speak directly with organization members and note follow-up meetings before choosing where to get involved.
cards.short_summary: Illinois Wesleyan’s registered organizations assemble together for one concentrated introduction.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan documents the RSO Fair as a fall tradition where registered student organizations gather to introduce involvement opportunities; its 2026 page schedules the fair for August 26 on the Quad.
cards.access_notes: The published 2026 RSO Involvement Fair is Wednesday, August 26, from 2:30–4:30 p.m. on the Quad.

cards.title: Walk the Campus Red Carpet
cards.subtitle: An annual formal celebration of campus cultures
cards.notes: Register when invitations open, dress for the announced theme and arrive early for student performances before the dancing begins.
cards.short_summary: Students, employees and alumni gather for a red-carpet evening built around cultural expression.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan announced its eighth annual Unity Gala for March 7, 2026, featuring cultural performances, food, dancing and celebration at Hansen Student Center, with free registration.
cards.source_title: Upcoming Unity Gala to Celebrate the Cultivation of Community
cards.access_notes: The documented 2026 event has concluded; future dates and registration requirements should be confirmed through the University.

cards.title: Spend Five Days Turning Titan
cards.subtitle: New students begin with a named fall-orientation rite
cards.notes: Plan to attend the full program, meet your first-year adviser and use Titan Orientation Leaders to learn campus resources.
cards.short_summary: Incoming students formally enter campus life through Illinois Wesleyan’s multi-day orientation program.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan describes Turning Titan as a multi-day fall program for community-building, advising and resource introductions and lists it as mandatory for first-year and transfer students.
cards.access_notes: The 2026 program runs August 19–23 for new students and August 20–23 for transfer students; no registration is required.

cards.title: Cheer for a Chariot-Born Titan
cards.subtitle: The gladiator mascot carries a campus-specific backstory
cards.notes: Spot Tommy at campus gatherings, then trace the character from a 1951 illustration to the photographed 1965 chariot entrance.
cards.short_summary: Illinois Wesleyan’s named gladiator mascot entered school lore with an actual Roman-style chariot appearance.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan credits alumnus Lee Short ’44 with creating Tommy’s gladiator image and name in 1951 and records Tommy’s 1965 football pregame entrance in a Roman-style chariot.
cards.access_notes: Mascot appearances vary by event; consult the relevant University or athletics schedule before planning a visit.

cards.title: Sing “Alma Wesleyana”
cards.subtitle: A school song preserved in the Titan songbook
cards.notes: Learn the brief alma mater from the University songbook and listen to the official Wind Ensemble arrangement before a campus ceremony.
cards.short_summary: The school’s ceremonial affection is expressed through a compact, century-spanning alma mater.
cards.evidence_claim: Illinois Wesleyan’s official traditions page publishes the words to “Alma Wesleyana” and provides an official songbook recording arranged by alumnus Peter Gilbert ’98.
cards.access_notes: The lyrics and recordings are publicly available; live performance depends on the ceremony or campus event.
